arguments.sql: SELECT m.mcc, c.description, COUNT(*) AS labelled_transactions, SUM(f.is_fraud) AS fraud_transactions, 1.0 * SUM(f.is_fraud) / COUNT(*) AS fraud_rate FROM transactions t JOIN fraud_labels f ON f.transaction_id = CAST(t.id AS TEXT) JOIN merchants m ON m.id = t.merchant_id LEFT JOIN mcc_codes c ON c.mcc = m.mcc GROUP BY m.mcc, c.description HAVING SUM(f.is_fraud) >= 50 ORDER BY fraud_rate DESC, m.mcc
arguments.explanation: For each merchant category code with at least 50 labelled fraud transactions, this shows its description, how many labelled transactions it has, how many of those are fraud, and its fraud rate. The rate is worked out over labelled transactions only, and the list is sorted from highest rate to lowest.
assumptions: Fraud rate is calculated only over transactions that have a fraud label. Transactions with no label are left out rather than counted as legitimate.
The '50 fraud transactions' cut-off counts transactions with is_fraud = 1.
Each transaction's MCC comes from its merchant (transactions.merchant_id -> merchants.mcc).
